subject.title: [Bug]: Local memory indexer (llama-cpp-provider) hangs indefinitely at 0 chunks

question: Can maintainers reproduce the local GGUF indexing hang on current main and identify whether the fix belongs in node-llama runtime options, worker abort handling, retry bounds, or memory-core commit/progress diagnostics?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the reported 50-minute high-CPU hang is not live-reproduced and the shipped timeout path already existed in a reported affected release.

options.title: Reproduce before repair
options.body: Capture a live local-provider `memory index --force` run with logs/process evidence, then route the fix to the proven failing layer.

options.title: Add diagnostics first
options.body: Use the related worker-lifecycle logging request to improve observability before attempting behavior changes.

options.title: Attempt speculative timeout repair
options.body: Patch abort/retry handling without live proof, accepting a higher risk of missing the actual node-llama or worker state failure.

recommendation.title: Reproduce before repair
recommendation.body: Capture a live local-provider `memory index --force` run with logs/process evidence, then route the fix to the proven failing layer.

likelyOwner.reason: The current local llama provider boundary and worker import path trace most directly through the local llama.cpp provider work.
